Israel's election produces no overall majority, leaving Arab parties as potential kingmakers

sources.body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition won the most seats in the general election but fell eight short of a parliamentary majority, final results showed Friday. Arab party groupings emerged as potential kingmakers, while allegations of foreign interference threatened to complicate efforts to form a government.
sources.headline: Netanyahu bloc in lead without majority in Israel election, say official results

sources.body:
Opposition explores options to form coalition as no party secures the 61 seats required for parliamentary majority.

Vote counting is complete in Israel’s elections with neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition winning a majority in parliament, Israeli media have said.

As the provisional results were being published on Thursday, opposition politicians met to explore options for a coalition.

With more than 99 percent of Tuesday’s ballots tallied, Netanyahu’s bloc held 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset while the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot secured 48 seats, Israeli outlet Haaretz reported. The Arab list parties, meanwhile, held a combined 19 seats, it added.

Both Netanyahu’s bloc and the opposition parties fell short of securing the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority.

The final results of the Knesset elections will be certified and announced by Wednesday. Until that date, the results are subject to change.

Tuesday’s elections – the first since the October 7, 2023, attacks on southern Israel and the start of Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza – were widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s premiership.

On Thursday, Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, met former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, who leads the Together party, to discuss ways to form a new government “as quickly as possible”, according to a statement reported by Israel’s Ynet News outlet.

Eisenkot also met Democrats party chairman Yair Golan, the only member of the opposition alliance to support forming a coalition with parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel, while all other political groups have rejected any such union.

Golan met separately with Mansour Abbas, who leads the United Arab list, or Ra’am, which is projected to win eight of the 19 Arab party seats.

“This is a time for action. Our responsibility is not to miss the opportunity for change and the salvation of Israel,” Golan said in a post on X after his meeting with Abbas.

Al Jazeera correspondent Nour Odeh noted that “Eisenkot has an uphill battle ahead of him.”

The former military leader-turned-politician has pledged “not to ally himself or get into a partnership with the Palestinian Israeli parties”, Odeh said, reporting from the occupied West Bank because Al Jazeera is banned from Israel.

But given the fact that no political bloc has a majority, the Eisenkot-led opposition bloc cannot form a governing coalition without the support of Arab-led parties, she added.

Meanwhile, Netanyahu’s Likud party has continued to amplify unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance – claims that have been rejected .

The head of the Central Elections Committee, Supreme Court Justice Noam Sohlberg, said “serious suspicions” of foreign interference had been brought to him in a letter to the Shin Bet security agency. Sohlberg said he could not verify the claims, but given their serious nature, he asked the agency to investigate.

Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of working to delegitimise the election results with his allegations.
sources.headline: Israel election result shows no overall majority as vote count complete

sources.body:
The main Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot and Arab-led party leaders have denounced Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for alleging foreign interference following the election which saw his coalition lose its majority.

Netanyahu's Likud accused Israel's Arab-led parties of "stealing" the election. Home security agency Shin Bet is investigating whether they received illegal funding from Qatar and Turkey.

Qatar's foreign ministry denied the "ridiculous and dangerous" allegations and accused Israeli politicians of conducting a disinformation campaign against Doha.

Final results confirmed that neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the Jewish opposition had won a majority in parliament.

The two Arab party lists - The Joint List and the Ra'am - defied expectations to win a record 19 seats in the 120-seat Knesset following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That positions them as potential kingmakers, with Netanyahu's bloc winning 53 seats and his rival Gadi Eisenkot's bloc securing 48.

On Thursday Likud alleged that voters had been "bribed" to vote for Arab parties, after the head of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) asked the Shin Bet security service to investigate "serious suspicions" of foreign interference.

Both Arab parties strongly rejected the claim, with the Arab-majority Joint List alliance saying it was baseless.

The row is being seen by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to delegitimise the Arab parties, thereby making it politically impossible for Eisenkot to join forces with them - which is currently his bloc's only route to power.

Israeli media reported that the CEC had been presented with a claim that Qatar had provided funding aimed at increasing voter turnout in Arab communities. Qatar's Foreign Ministry "categorically" denied the claims.

Netanyahu and his Likud Party framed the allegations as a "political earthquake" and an "an attack on democracy", aimed at removing their right-wing government.

But the Shin Bet later clarified that their investigation did not implicate an entire community who had voted legally, while acting CEC Director General Dean Livne said there was "no basis for allegations of systematic violations of election integrity."

Eisenkot, who was briefed on the investigation, said "it is too early to determine what happened, or if anything happened at all," and accused Netanyahu of running "an orchestrated and organized campaign to delegitimize the election results".

Balad chairman Sami Abu Shehadeh, who is part of the Joint List, dismissed the allegation, saying: "The losing side is constructing a racist blood libel and calling on the security agencies to use force in order to overturn the election results."

Netanyahu's attacks on Arab voters and parties have been ongoing for days. He spent much of election day posting on social media that high Arab turnout is an "emergency" and a "matter of life or death" for the Israeli right. He also shared AI-generated images of Arab voters at polling stations, in an attempt to encourage right-wingers to get out and vote.
sources.headline: Israeli opposition accuses Netanyahu of trying to 'delegitimise' election

stories.headline: Binance says a security breach affected $6.3 billion in assets in a potential record crypto heist

sources.body: Binance said on Thursday that a security breach had affected an estimated $6.3 billion in assets, potentially making it the biggest cryptocurrency heist on record. The world's largest crypto exchange said it had recovered or frozen about $3 billion, while the incident sent Bitcoin and other digital currencies lower.
sources.headline: Binance security breach has $6.3 billion impact in potential record crypto heist

sources.body:
Blockchain intelligence firm attributes attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers.

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has said that about $6.3bn in funds have been stolen in a “security incident” that looks to be the biggest crypto heist in history.

The world’s largest crypto exchange said on Thursday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3bn in funds had been frozen following the apparent hacking.

Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorised transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.

The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.

“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement to Al Jazeera.

“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”

The company added that it would share a “detailed” technical post-mortem once investigations were complete.

Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and largest shareholder, said earlier that the exchange appeared to have been hacked.

TRM, a blockchain intelligence firm, said in a report that it assessed with “high confidence” that the attack was carried out by North Korea’s hacking unit TraderTraitor, which investigators have linked to the Lazarus Group.

Ari Redbord, TRM’s global head of policy, described the attack as “unprecedented” and a “watershed”.

“When North Korea steals at this scale, the money funds weapons proliferation and other destabilising activity. That makes this a global security issue, not just a crypto theft,” Redbord told Al Jazeera.

The price of Bitcoin, the world’s most popular cryptocurrency, fell about 5 percent following the heist, dropping below $77,000.

“Binance is one of the largest centralised exchanges, and so a blow to confidence in them risks shocking confidence to many retail investors, which could dampen prices of crypto assets,” Sean Foley, an expert in crypto markets at Macquarie University in Sydney, told Al Jazeera.

Foley said the attack highlighted the risks of centralised exchanges and could spur more traders to use decentralised alternatives.

“Any assets held at a centralised exchange are only as safe as the exchange itself, and the larger the exchange’s holdings, the larger a target it becomes,” Foley said.

The Binance hacking dwarfs the previous record for a crypto theft, set in 2025 when North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group carried out a $1.5bn heist on Bybit.

Cybercriminals stole $2.87bn in crypto assets in nearly 150 hacking incidents in 2025, according to the 2026 Crypto Crime Report produced by TRM.

Binance, founded in China by Zhao in 2017, has about $155bn in assets under management, more than any other exchange, according to CoinMarketCap.
sources.headline: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history

sources.body:
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what has been described as the "largest hack in history".

The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets have been frozen with the help of other platforms, adding that it will "cover all losses".

Early checks show the incident may have involved an engineer's laptop that had been compromised, which allowed an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.

AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs has attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025 , to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.

"We make this judgment with high confidence," TRM said in a report, adding that several elements of the attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.

The lab's chief policy officer Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.

The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.

Binance did not directly respond to BBC queries about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."

The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.

In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.

"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.

Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.

Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident.

Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."

"Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT.

World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.

Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.

Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.

Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
sources.headline: Crypto giant Binance hit by 'largest hack in history'

stories.headline: China expels a record number of Communist Party members amid Xi Jinping's intensified purges

sources.body:
The unprecedented number of empty seats at the fifth plenum – a symbol of expulsions – serve as a symbol for the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping

China expelled a record number of officials from the Chinese Communist party (CCP) as it concluded a major political gathering , which saw an unprecedented number of empty seats indicating the scale of the purges under Xi Jinping.

A record 33 members were expelled at this week’s fifth plenum, a gathering of top officials that takes place roughly once a year.

Just 279 of the full and alternate members of the CCP’s Central Committee attended this week’s gathering, compared with the 376 originally named as members in 2022. That means that more than 25% of the original cohort were absent, many due to purges. It is the highest number of “empty chairs” at the plenum in modern Chinese history.

The confirmed expulsions included Zhang Youxia, the former second-in-command to China’s leader in the military hierarchy, and Ma Xingrui, the former party secretary for Xinjiang. Other absences were unexplained.

“More empty seats underscores the plenum’s focus on Xi’s vision of strict internal discipline,” said Neil Thomas, a senior fellow at the Asia Society thinktank, in a post on X.

The theme for this week’s plenum was party governance. Since coming to power in 2012 Xi has focused on stamping out corruption in the party. But in recent years the campaign has intensified , taking out officials in the highest ranks of the party and the military, raising questions about if the campaign is also a tool to remove political rivals or punish disloyalty.

Xi appears to have grown increasingly frustrated with what he sees as a lack of discipline in the ranks of the party that wields absolute authority over the state and society in China. Earlier this year he said that the party must uproot “sick trees” and that the fight against corruption was a “never-ending journey”.

A series of purges has gutted the seven-man Central Military Commission, the ruling body of China’s People’s Liberation Army. There are now just two members left: Xi himself, and the military’s anti-graft tsar, Zhang Shengmin.

Zhang was promoted to the politburo of the CCP this week, the highest ruling body in the party. Zhang is now the only military member of the senior leadership body.

The plenum also laid the groundwork for the 21st Party congress, an event which happens every five years and is expected to next be held in the second half of 2027. Xi is expected to secure a fourth term as leader of the party, making him the longest ruler of Communist China since Mao Zedong.

The ranks of the Central Committee and the politburo will be refreshed at next year’s congress, but many analysts believe that recent purges have been so wide-ranging that there are few suitable candidates to be promoted.
sources.headline: China expels a record number from Communist party amid Xi’s intensified purges of top officials

sources.body:
A record 33 members have been expelled from China's Communist Party as it concluded a major annual political gathering, which had the most empty seats ever seen.

The fifth plenum was attended by 279 Central Committee members, compared to 315 at the fourth plenum in October 2025 and 364 at the third one in July 2024.

While recent plenums focused on economic reforms or social and development issues, party discipline took centre stage at this week's gathering.

Xi Jinping has made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his rule since he took the reins in 2012, calling it the "biggest threat" to the party.

Since then, more than two million individuals have been disciplined for cases related to "pointless formalities, bureaucratism, hedonism and extravagance", Zhang Fuhai, from the party's disciplinary commission, told a press briefing on Friday.

He also said the party would enhance its efforts to ensure officials "dare not, cannot, and do not want to be corrupt".

Sixteen of the 33 members expelled are from the military, according to a communique issued on Thursday, which marked the end of the four-day closed-door gathering held at a hotel in Beijing.

It's unclear what specific charges these members face beyond "serious disciplinary and legal violations". Such broad allegations have become routine under Xi's anti-corruption campaign.

It has now become "an effort to consolidate and maintain authority", says Chong Ja Ian, a non-resident scholar with Carnegie China.

"In this case, the campaign will continue and expand depending on how secure Xi feels rather than any real issue with corruption."

In its statement, the party said it has "squarely confronted the grim reality that party leadership had at times weakened or hollowed out" and that it will continue to "enforce strict party self-governance, including turning the knife inwards to... curb disorder".

The latest expulsions bring the total number of members removed under Xi's third term to a record 51, up from 35 and five in his first and second terms respectively.

Beyond the plenum, China's top anti-corruption watchdog reported that 680,000 people across the party apparatus have been disciplined in the first nine months of this year.

This is also the first time in Xi's 14 years of leadership that plenum attendance fell below 300. The current Central Committee started its term in 2022 with more than 370 members.

Observers argue that Xi views corruption not just as graft but also ideological impurity and, crucially, disloyalty.

In January, he warned against "two-faced cadres" who profess political loyalty but defy orders and act in their self-interest.

Among the high-ranking officials expelled are former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui, and ex-top generals Zhang Youxia and Liu Zhenli. Official statements announcing their removal this year said they "seriously violating [the party's] discipline and rules", which is widely read as a euphemism for corruption.

The culling of the military's top brass has been particularly significant, with Neil Thomas, Lobsang Tsering and Shengyu Wang from the Asia Society Policy Institute describing it as "in a category of its own".
sources.headline: Record number of purges as Xi emphasises 'party discipline' at China political gathering

stories.headline: North Korea tests attack drones as Kim Jong Un calls for faster AI-enabled military development

sources.body: North Korea has tested attack drones, cruise missiles and rocket launchers at a weapons demonstration, state media reported Friday, as Kim Jong Un called for faster development of military drone and artificial intelligence technology. The tests follow a series of weapons trials and rising tensions with South Korea.
sources.headline: North Korea tests attack drones as Kim calls for 'absolute superiority'

stories.headline: Christine Lagarde says she will step down early as European Central Bank president to regain freedom to speak out

sources.body:
Possible candidate to run World Economic Forum departs ECB nine months early, saying she wants to speak her mind about world affairs

Christine Lagarde, the eurozone’s top central banker, has said she is stepping down nine months early to speak her mind about world affairs and confront the “misrepresentation of the truth”.

Ending months of speculation about her future at the European Central Bank , Lagarde said she would quit her role as president in March rather than October next year because the rules of neutrality that governed her job prevented her from influencing debate about financial and economics affairs.

She spoke at the end of a press conference to explain the ECB’s decision to hold interest rates – maintaining its key deposit rate at 2.5% – despite inflation climbing to 3.8% last month, its highest since September 2023.

Lagarde said: “I ‌want to have the freedom of speech, the freedom of expression and the freedom ‌to engage on matters that are not monetary policy matters.”

The former managing director of the International Monetary Fund has been tipped as a candidate to take over the running of the World Economic Forum, which holds its annual meeting in Davos each January. The WEF founder, Klaus Schwab, stepped down last year after being accused of financial and ethical misconduct, which he denies.

Lagarde’s early departure fires the starting gun on the race to replace her as ECB chief, at a time when the eurozone is struggling with weak growth and above-target inflation. Potential candidates include the former Dutch central bank president Klaas Knot, the Spanish banker Pablo Hernández de Cos, the German central bank president, Joachim Nagel, and Nadia Calviño, the president of the European Investment Bank.

The European Council made up of EU heads of state appoints the head of the ECB , which sets monetary policy across the eurozone.

There has been speculation that Lagarde, a former finance minister of France , has been encouraged to quit early by the French president, Emmanuel Macron, so her successor can be appointed before the possibility of a far-right or far-left presidential candidate being elected to the Élysée Palace. Lagarde will also be able to participate in next April’s elections.

She noted that ECB officials were bound by strict rules on not appearing partisan. “We have an obligation of neutrality; we comment on the situation with the focus on monetary policy,” Lagarde said, adding that the mandate was “the price we pay for being independent”.

Lagarde said she no longer ‌felt comfortable staying silent on broader global issues. “I’m interested in the truth, and I see the truth being very often damaged, contradicted by misrepresentation,” she ​said, without elaborating.

Drawing on more than two decades in international economic and financial roles, she said she had more to contribute. “There are things that I can say – whether people will listen or not is another story. But I feel that I ⁠should say those things and I cannot do so in my current ​position.”
sources.headline: Europe’s central bank chief, Christine Lagarde, steps down for ‘freedom of speech’

stories.headline: Trump and Republican attacks on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed raise fears of anti-Muslim backlash

sources.body: DEARBORN, MICHIGAN — “A threat to America.” “Radical ideology.” “A jihadist.” President Donald Trump and Republicans are ratcheting up their efforts to brand Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, a Michigan-born Muslim whose parents emigrated from Egypt, as an “extremist” in the final days of the state’s critical Senate race. It has sparked concern among some El-Sayed supporters, who fear the deluge of attacks could break through to some undecided voters. It has infuriated some of the president’s one-time Muslim and Arab allies in the state with the largest concentration of Arab Americans in the country, who view the comments as Islamophobic and racist. And it has caused some of them to lose hope in Republicans. “You turned off a lot of people. Even people that were working to get Trump elected and get people to vote Republican here have flipped. We did all this work for them to turn around and use us as enemies, to be able just to win an election,” said Hassan Nehme, a GOP statehouse candidate and former Michigan Republican Party vice chair who helped lead Arab American outreach for the GOP in 2024. He is undecided in how he’ll vote in this year’s Senate race. “It's to the point [where] I'm like, why am I even fighting to be in this party?” Republicans’ increasingly incendiary rhetoric in the crucial Senate race is overshadowing the close of an already polarizing election. “Michigan is a battleground. That’s the truth. And racism is real,” Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud, a Democrat in an Arab-majority city who is backing El-Sayed , said in an interview at his office Tuesday. “If you have folks who refuse to vote for somebody because of the direction in which they pray, it most certainly has an impact.” Hammoud believes most voters will see past it. But Republicans are bearing down. Trump, who has repeatedly mocked and mispronounced El-Sayed’s name, labeled him a “jihadist” during a rally for GOP nominee Mike Rogers in Port Huron this past Sunday and said he would “be unable to get a seat on an airplane.” Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., in a campaign event with Rogers in Grand Rapids on Monday, claimed the world’s 500 million Arabs no longer produce award-winning science or literature and instead create “stagnant societies that do two things — hatred and war and victimization.” Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas), while campaigning for Rogers in Michigan on Wednesday, called El-Sayed a “jihadist leprechaun.” Ads from Rogers’ campaign and allied GOP groups attacking El-Sayed in this vein run in rotation across Michigan television. Senate Leadership Fund , the top GOP Senate super PAC, says El-Sayed gets “dirty money” from an “Islamic extremist group” that is “tied to Hamas.” Rogers, in a direct-to-camera clip , calls El-Sayed “a threat to America.” Bishara Bahbah, an Arizona resident who founded Arab Americans for Trump and helped facilitate Trump’s 2024 outreach to Michigan’s Arab community, said Trump’s Sunday comments cross “a red line.” “The only consequence that I can see from these comments is a complete reversal of the support in Michigan and other states where Arabs and Muslims vote, toward the Democratic Party.” Rogers has been more specific in how he’s gone after his opponent. He has attacked El-Sayed for taking campaign donations from donors affiliated with the Council on American-Islamic Relations , a Muslim advocacy group, which Republicans have long attacked as a terrorist group even though the U.S. government has not designated it as such. He’s alleged ties between El-Sayed’s family and the Muslim Brotherhood, in part through El-Sayed’s father-in-law’s involvement with CAIR and the Islamic Society of North America , another Muslim group . El-Sayed’s campaign referred to past statements from both CAIR and ISNA denying affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. Rogers has also referenced El-Sayed’s mother’s work for a charity that the Bush administration classified as a supporter of terrorist groups , as reported by The New York Times.   El-Sayed has disavowed the Muslim Brotherhood and said his family has “no” ties to it . El-Sayed’s parents separated when he was three years old, and he says he was raised by his father and stepmother. His campaign responded to Trump’s rally in a statement saying while Trump and Rogers “lie and resort to desperate, bad faith attacks, Abdul remains laser focused on his plans to bring down costs and stand up to the chaos and corruption in Washington.” “I’m not worried,” El-Sayed told reporters at a Detroit union hall on Monday, “because just like I did 18 months ago when I kicked off this campaign, I am taking a bet on the bigness of Michiganders.” And President Barack Obama, in a rally with El-Sayed in Detroit on Saturday, said: “This stuff didn’t work on me, not in Michigan. It’s not going to work on Abdul.” But some of El-Sayed’s allies are concerned. James Tate, president of the Detroit City Council noted that El-Sayed “can’t defend himself in every household." El-Sayed’s campaign and his allies are fighting back by knocking on doors and hitting the airwaves, a sign they’re cognizant the attacks could have an impact. One El-Sayed ad features his white step-grandparents responding to some of Trump’s attacks. “Communist? We’re Presbyterian!" his grandparents say in the spot . El-Sayed cut another ad featuring images of a menorah and of him praying with Black parishioners. “His faith — I think that scares some people,” said Dana Harris, the regional director of the Coalition of Black Trade Unionists, who was doorknocking for El-Sayed across northwest Detroit last Saturday. “But at the end of the day. he’s a human being like the rest of us. And he wants change.” Rogers and his allies say questioning ties to extremist organizations doesn’t equate to Islamophobia. Rogers’ campaign referred POLITICO to comments he made ahead of Trump and Kennedy’s events . “This is not about Islam. It's not about how he prays,” Rogers said on NBC’s “Meet the Press” Sunday morning. “It is about his adherence to this radical Islamic agenda.” In a statement, White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said Trump “will continue to unapologetically fight for American greatness and call out extremists like Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed without apology.” CORRECTION: Dana Harris is the regional director of the Coalition of Black Trade Unionists.
sources.headline: El-Sayed’s allies fear Trump’s anti-Muslim attacks are reaching undecided voters

sources.body:
Muslim advocates say the best way to respond to hate is to elect the Democratic candidate in Michigan to US Senate.

Al Jazeera speaks to El-Sayed as religion becomes flashpoint in Senate race

Dearborn, Michigan – Jake Lang, a far-right provocateur in a bulletproof vest, shouts anti-Muslim obscenities on a bullhorn outside a rally featuring former US President Barack Obama in Detroit.

His associates, wearing crusader-themed accessories – including a tin shield featuring a black cross – hold campaign signs for Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate in Michigan, who is in a close race with Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

If it weren’t for the bigoted slogans, the people lining up around them to attend the campaign event for El-Sayed and other Democrats could have mistakenly thought the protesters were in Halloween costumes.

“Get the f*** out, Muslims,” Lang shouted. “The crusade is coming. Self-deport.”

Lang may appear like a fringe agitator. But Muslim American activists say the bigotry he is spreading is going mainstream, especially in the context of the Senate race in Michigan.

Anti-Muslim attacks against El-Sayed have been perpetuated at the highest level of the US government, including by President Donald Trump and his cabinet members.

Suehaila Amen, a prominent Arab and Muslim advocate in the Detroit area, said bigotry against her community is reaching an all-time high.

“They make immediately post 9/11 look like a walk in the park for us. This has been absolutely disgusting to witness,” Amen told Al Jazeera.

One of Lang’s allies, Pastor Lorenzo Sewell, is an official faith adviser to the Rogers campaign.

Sewell helped Lang organise an anti-Muslim march in the Detroit suburb of Dearborn – home to a large Arab and Muslim community – in August.

Abdullah Hammoud , the mayor of Dearborn, said the city – which has long been a target for anti-Muslim provocateurs – has been receiving an increased number of threats in recent months.

“The general public is unaware of how many threats are aimed towards the city of Dearborn on a daily basis, via social [media], via our dispatch when they’re calling 911 or calling our call centre, and lobbing these threats against the residents of the city each and every single day,” Hammoud told Al Jazeera.

While the Rogers campaign did not respond to Al Jazeera’s request for comment about the Republican candidate’s links to Sewell, Rogers defended his focus on El-Sayed’s background, saying it was for national security.

“This is not about the way you pray; it’s the way you think,” Rogers told reporters after his debate with El-Sayed earlier this month.

Local leaders say their community is not cowering in the face of such threats and Trump’s near-daily attacks, and is pushing back through civic engagement and rallying around the El-Sayed campaign.

“Trump is a fascist,” Hammoud told Al Jazeera. “I think the best thing we can do, the best response, is to send Abdul to the US Senate, somebody who’s got two doctorates, someone who is a son of this country, a son of the state, someone who is the captain of his high school team … I think that that’s the best response that we can give fascism.”
sources.headline: US Muslims concerned but resilient as ‘hate’ attacks target Abdul El-Sayed

stories.headline: Democrats make a late push for rural Midwest districts as tariffs, energy prices and the Iran war weigh on voters

sources.body: EAU CLAIRE, Wisconsin — In this rural-heavy stretch of the upper Midwest, Democrats are trying to claw back districts where their party brand is still deeply toxic. It won’t be easy, even in a midterm environment that heavily favors their party. Local Democratic organizers in western Wisconsin, where Rebecca Cooke is trying to oust GOP Rep. Derrick Van Orden, know that elections here are decided by the slimmest of margins. They have no room for error. “Everything's on a razor's edge,” Clara Serrano, who volunteers for the local Democratic Party, said as she drove along farms and cornfields outside Eau Claire. But a decade after President Donald Trump’s populism and culture wars swung the formerly Democratic-leaning region right, many voters from western Wisconsin over to southern Minnesota and down to eastern Iowa are hurting — and blame the president’s policies. Family farms are reeling from his tariffs. Diesel is over $6 a gallon. The cost of fertilizer has shot up more than 30 percent since the war in Iran began earlier this year. “[Rural voters are] mad when we get to the door — and not at us,” said William Garcia, co-chair of the La Crosse County Democratic Party who has been out canvassing. “They're mad about gas prices. They're mad about fertilizer. They're mad about the tariffs. And so all we do as Democrats is say, ‘Hey, we agree. We rejected all of these things. We've been fighting all of these things.’ So it’s much more receptive now than really it's ever been.” Local Democrats have pulled out all the stops to propel Cooke in Wisconsin’s 3rd District, knocking endless doors in redder areas . There have been national reinforcements as well: Populist Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) endorsed Cooke during the primary and hit the campaign trail with her this week in Eau Claire. The national party is trying to make generational gains in Minnesota’s 1st District — where they’re hoping to pull off a major upset to unseat GOP Rep. Brad Finstad in a Trump +12 district — and in deep-red Iowa, where Democrats are targeting three GOP House seats, a Senate seat and the governorship. Democrats for years have faltered with rural voters in these districts. Now, with polling showing Democrats gaining ground in redder territory and an electorate that’s souring on the GOP, Democrats hope they can finally make up ground this November — and lay a solid foundation for the 2028 presidential election. If that doesn’t happen, it’s an ominous sign for the party. “If we can’t win these seats now in this environment, it seems like we’re in for a world of hurt in 2028,” said one House Democrat, who, like others in this article, was granted anonymity to speak candidly. Wisconsin Democrats have worked nearly-year round to build up a ground game. A major new initiative from the state party has helped to boost organizing, especially in rural counties and other places they’ve struggled. “We haven't really stopped organizing since 2024,” said Pete Huff, co-chair of the nearby Dunn County Democratic party, where Trump won by 16 points. Cooke, who grew up on a farm in the area, has tried to create a more durable brand of politics in the district by largely trying to distance herself from the national Democratic party as she seeks to win over a broader base of voters. It helped in 2024: She overperformed Kamala Harris by 9,000 votes across the district, even though she narrowly lost to Van Orden. “I think that the party doesn't know how to speak the language of rural America, and I feel like I uniquely do,” Cooke said in an interview. She regularly canvasses in rural communities and has tried to tie Van Orden to increasingly unpopular data center developments, after local projects sparked backlash. On Sunday, before the campus rally, Cooke attended a meeting for residents worried about a new high-voltage transmission line that would cut through farmland. This cycle, she’s especially leaned into the rare House endorsement from Sanders, who’s built his own populist and anti-establishment brand. At a Sunday rally on the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire campus, she introduced the Vermont senator by saying: “Everyone forgets he’s an independent.” Potential 2028 Democratic presidential contenders see the stakes of winning back rural-heavy districts as well. Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg is traveling to Minnesota’s 1st District on Sunday to rally voters for Democrat Jake Johnson in Rochester. It’s one of the many once-safe red seats that Republicans and Trump’s political operation are scrambling to shore up in these final days, with Johnson and Finstad running in what’s become a highly competitive race. Minnesota’s Democratic Gov. Tim Walz, then a high school teacher, won a House seat here in a 2006 wave election amid voter anger at the Iraq war and their GOP incumbent. Also that year, a local prosecutor named Amy Klobuchar swept to a big Senate win, part of a Democratic surge across the region. Democrats are hopeful that history is repeating, with high costs and a president unpopular because of a Middle East incursion hurting the GOP in the region and nationally. “The price of diesel is devastating,” said Ted Winter, who farms with his son near Fulda. “We've patterned a lot of our campaign after Amy Klobuchar, who famously shows up in every single county every single year,” Johnson, a math teacher, said in an interview. “And so I just said, ‘hey guys, let's host a town hall in every county.’” National Republicans for months brushed off concerns from local Republicans that Finstad’s race was growing increasingly competitive. Pro-Trump super PACs only recently injected their first cash of the race into the district, with the latest total quickly hitting several million dollars — an unheard-of prospect just a few weeks ago. The National Republican Congressional Committee spent for the first time in the race Tuesday. Democratic groups, on the other hand, started spending in the contest over the summer — and the leading House Democratic super PAC just responded with a $2.2 million money dump and a last-minute TV ad campaign . Finstad said in an interview at a local textile mill in Faribault that he flagged money concerns to national Republicans weeks ago. He also raised those concerns to GOP Whip Tom Emmer, who is from Minnesota. “We raised that with anybody and everybody that would want to hear it,” Finstad said. “From a global perspective, people were like, ‘Well, you won by 18, you're fine.’ And, you know, those of us in Minnesota know that this district has always had kind of an independent streak to it.” But Finstad said the tariffs were helping farmers in some cases, and the massive fraud scandals in Minnesota are keeping Trump voters and Republicans engaged in the final days. That’s one particular drag that could hit Johnson in this area. Democrats are still optimistic. “Things are changing in rural America right now,” Klobuchar, who’s now running for governor, told a crowd of volunteers and voters alongside Johnson on Sunday, at a local park in Fairmont. She pointed not only to the tightening 1st District race, but also to neighboring Iowa as proof. Republicans have grown particularly worried about the Hawkeye State as they’ve privately come to believe Democrats will flip at least one of three congressional seats there. And, they’re alarmed about the prospect of wider losses across a state Trump won by 13 percentage points, should disillusioned Republican voters decide not to turn out in the numbers they need.“Does it feel good to be running neck-and-neck against Democrats in Iowa just days out? No,” said one GOP strategist in Iowa working on a House race. But they noted that long-term demographic make-up of most Iowa districts do not favor Democrats. Speaker Mike Johnson is traveling to Rep. Zach Nunn’s Des Moines-based district in Iowa on Wednesday to help save the seat. Republican Joe Mitchell, who is running in the nearby seat to replace GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson, is locked within the margin of error in his race against Democrat Lindsay James, according to two people with direct knowledge of internal polls. And Republicans are largely assuming GOP Rep. Mariannette Miller Meeks’ seat just to the south of that is already gone as she faces Democrat Christina Bohannan. “The tariffs, the Iran war, the health care cuts, these things are just brutal for the people of Southeast Iowa,” Bohannan said in an interview. That’s why national and local Democrats alike worry if they can’t pull out key wins in the upper Midwest this election season, they will continue to be shut out of power for years. They’re keenly aware that, no matter how frustrated rural voters are with Republicans, they’re still wary of the national Democratic party brand. “I don’t approach the door as a Democrat,” Jeremiah Fredrickson, who’s running to flip a Wisconsin state assembly seat, said in an interview before he knocked doors in the small, GOP-leaning village of Elk Mound. “My goal is to try to be a representative. I think way too many of our politicians have gotten to the point where they go to Madison, and they forget about the people back here.” At one door, an older man with white hair looked down at the pamphlet Serrano — the Democratic volunteer for Cooke and Fredrickson — was holding. “You can keep that,” he replied. “I’m not voting for them. No way in hell.” Van Orden, the Wisconsin Republican racing to hold his seat against Cooke, is skeptical his district’s voters will swing back toward Democrats. That’s despite high prices and Trump’s current unfavorability.   The retired Navy SEAL rode in on his Harley-Davidson motorcycle to the Boon Docks bar as part of a multi-day district tour. After greeting patrons, he told POLITICO in an interview that Cooke is a “flat-out socialist.” He dismissed Sanders’ draw, saying that “voters here hate career politicians." “Is it politically convenient that we're fighting with the Iranians now? The answer is no,” Van Orden said. “I don't want gas prices to go up. I also don’t want my grandkids fighting the Iranians … 50 years from now.” But he’s counting on Trump voters to turn out for him. Across the bar, Deb Bork, who’s in her 70s and lives up the road in the small town of Independence, said she was sticking with Van Orden and Trump, regardless of the “hardship” of higher gas prices, saying the war was a blip compared to the length of other U.S. wars. She still trusts Trump. “He feels it's in the best interest of our country to protect us,” she added. “For so long we've been out there protecting everybody else and forgetting about the people that live here.”

In Arkansas, rising costs spurred farmer Hallie Shoffner’s long-shot Senate campaign. Will farmers back her?

When Paul McKinney, a farmer in northeast Arkansas, thinks of his son’s childhood, he remembers a small boy playing in vast fields.

To a child, a flooded rice field is “like a giant, 40-acre swimming pool”, he said.

Rice has been a staple on McKinney’s farm for four generations. Next year, however, the family plans to plant much less. Instead, they will focus on soya, a crop that is cheaper to produce.

Like farmers across the United States , McKinney is making tough decisions this year in response to higher fuel and fertiliser costs, which have skyrocketed since the start of the war on Iran.

This week, farmers also face tough choices at the polls. Democrats are expected to make gains in the midterm elections, as voters react to high prices economy-wide by switching parties or staying home.

Observers are watching farm country closely. Texas and Kansas could send Democrats to the Senate for the first time in decades. In the House of Representatives, two majority-rural districts, Wisconsin’s Third and North Carolina First, could become tipping points for Democratic control.

Still, many of the country’s most rural areas, like Arkansas, are also its most safely Republican.

That leaves an uphill battle for Democrat Hallie Shoffner, who quit farming last year to challenge Republican Senator Tom Cotton in a campaign squarely focused on rising costs.

Even before the US-Israel war on Iran, high input costs were straining farmers, said Ryan Loy, an extension economist for the University of Arkansas’ Division of Agriculture.

Loy pointed to a trade war with China that began in 2018, the ongoing war in Ukraine and disruptions related to the 2025 tariffs as factors driving up input costs and disrupting markets. A drought across the US heartland, made worse by climate change, has added to the strain.

Farmers across the country are working to adapt. In Arkansas, many farmers skipped rice in favour of soya. Soya is “the least input-intensive crop, and perhaps can break even or have the shallowest loss”, Loy said.

Now Arkansas, usually the country’s top rice producer, has its lowest rice acreage since the 1970s. Many farmers hoped 2026 would bring economic recovery so they could return to rice.

Then, the war on Iran hit. With the Strait of Hormuz blocked, fertiliser costs jumped just as farmers were fertilising during the spring planting season.

Loy tracked the increase in a sample budget that he maintains for Arkansas row crop farmers. “Urea fertiliser specifically peaked about 39 percent over our budgeted amount,” Loy said. Diesel costs came in about 72 percent more than budget averaged across the planting, growing and harvesting seasons, Loy found.

Those changes represent a significant economic hit. “For our state alone, it’s an additional cost of about $343m,” Loy said.

Last week, US President Donald Trump announced an $8bn fuel relief programme for farmers, following $12bn in tariff-related aid in 2025. If the fuel relief payment were divided equally between the 50 states, it would cover less than half of the extra costs that Loy estimates Arkansas’ farmers paid this year.
sources.headline: As US midterms approach, farmers decide what to plant and how to vote

stories.headline: Turning Point USA's heavy investment in Arizona Republican Andy Biggs faces a pivotal test in the governor's race

sources.body: Turning Point USA has gone all-in to make GOP Rep. Andy Biggs the next governor of Arizona, their top priority of the cycle. It appears they will come up short. Biggs was the last candidate Turning Point founder Charlie Kirk personally endorsed before he was killed one year ago. Kirk himself recruited the longtime ally in their home state to run for governor this cycle — and Turning Point has since spent $18 million, the most they’ve dropped for anyone this cycle, to try to salvage his campaign. “It's a legacy thing for them,” said former Rep. Matt Salmon (R-Ariz.). “This is their swan song. This is kind of all-or-nothing for them.” But Biggs, a former chair of the hardline House Freedom Caucus and close ally of President Donald Trump who previously served as Arizona Senate president, has trailed Democratic Gov. Katie Hobbs in virtually every public poll of the race this year, most of them outside the margin of error. And some Arizona Republicans have been baffled by Turning Point’s strategy. The group faces immense criticism from within the state GOP for delaying its biggest spending until September, just weeks before ballots were sent out, according to conversations with 10 local operatives and officials. Biggs’ race is the most high-stakes political test for Turning Point Action since Kirk’s 2025 death, and the result will have major implications for the group’s reputation and relevancy within the GOP moving forward. Turning Point has already preemptively endorsed Vice President JD Vance , who was particularly close to Kirk, for president. Should Vance decide to run, he could rely on Turning Point’s ground operation in swing states like Arizona and beyond. The group could well overperform this year, and if they are successful in lifting Biggs in their home state, it could send a signal. But a loss could have 2028 repercussions, too. “If JD Vance intends to run for president, I think it would be a good idea to reevaluate any thoughts he might have about utilizing Turning Point Action as his field operation,” said Gina Swoboda, a former chair of the Arizona Republican Party who has openly sparred with the organization. A spokesperson for Vance did not respond to a request for comment. Other Republicans, including the Biggs’ campaign, said they’re grateful that Turning Point didn’t wave the white flag in a tough year for the GOP, as voters reel from the impact of Trump’s policies. “Turning Point Action’s investments both on the ground and over the airwaves in Arizona have been tremendous. We are very grateful they’ve stepped up to support Andy and Republicans up and down the ballot in an extremely difficult environment,” Biggs campaign spokesperson Drew Sexton said in a statement. In a statement, Tyler Bowyer, chief operating officer of Turning Point Action, said he is “very proud of the strides we have made in Arizona and other swing states.” He emphasized TP Action is “a Get-Out-The-Vote (GOTV) centric organization” and not TV-focused, pointing the blame elsewhere. “It is the job of national apparatus groups to go on air early and support Republican nominees,” he said. “We of course are disappointed that more national Republican dollars are not matching the national Democrat dollars being spent on Presidential swing states like Arizona.” While the RGA has stayed out of the race, the Democratic Governors Association has spent at least $10 million . Hobbs, who was elected to the purple state’s governorship in 2022, launched her first general election TV ad in May , while Biggs was still focused on his late July primary. At the time, Turning Point mocked Hobbs for "spending like a drunken sailor" by launching spending so early. But now, Republicans say that Hobbs was able to entrench her lead in the race by spending early while Biggs was dark on the airwaves — and blame Turning Point along with other GOP outside groups like the Republican Governors Association for not spending earlier to keep the race competitive. The RGA declined to comment on their decision not to spend in the race. In a state like Arizona, where an incumbent governor hasn’t lost reelection since 1966 and some 80% of voters cast ballots before Election Day, a late deluge of cash is less likely to sway the race. “If you're spending that much money, a big portion of that would've been really helpful earlier in the race when Andy was completely broke, he didn't have two nickels to rub together, and Hobbs was dominating the airwaves with no response and beating the crap out of Andy,” said Salmon.”A lot of us are scratching our heads.” Biggs’ campaign reported just $1.26 million cash on hand in July, while Hobbs’ campaign reported double that . Many donors to former GOP Gov. Doug Ducey have stayed on the sidelines this year . One Republican operative working on other Arizona races, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said that at this point, “No amount of spending is going to change the fact that Biggs is going to lose.” “In all likelihood, the top statewide seats are going Democrat. And Turning Point owns it,” the strategist added. “They wanted to be the player. They wanted to be the guy. Guess what? They are.” Many local Republicans are frustrated that the RGA never spent a penny on the top race in a state Trump won in 2024. While Biggs was getting hammered early on the airwaves, the RGA was spending nearly $4 million on the Wisconsin Democratic primary to boost a democratic socialist who narrowly lost. For several cycles, Turning Point has muscled statewide candidates through messy Republican primaries, only to see them falter in November. In 2022, it pushed hardliners Blake Masters and Kari Lake as nominees for U.S. Senate and governor, only to see both lose. In 2024, they backed Lake’s bid for Senate; even as Trump won Arizona by five points, Lake lost by two. Biggs, some Republicans thought, would be different. He had high name ID statewide and a track record of public service for Arizona, both in the state Senate and the U.S. House. Kirk himself personally urged Biggs to enter the governor’s race, Biggs told the Arizona Republic , even though Trump had already endorsed Karrin Taylor Robson, a Phoenix attorney and businesswoman, early in the race. After Biggs entered the race in January 2025, Trump split his endorsement between Robson and Biggs — and Turning Point took a victory lap. “Turning Point Action will marshall our organization's full resources, ground game, and support behind the Biggs for Arizona campaign, and we’re honored to be able to do so,” Charlie Kirk said in a May 2025 statement . “He has my full and complete endorsement.” Robson later dropped out , and Turning Point helped Biggs romp to a massive victory in the primary. Next Tuesday will test if their general-election acumen has improved.
sources.headline: Turning Point rests its reputation on Andy Biggs’ race. It’s not looking good.

stories.headline: A judge blocks the Trump administration's Medicaid rule requiring some recipients to prove impairment

sources.body:
US District Judge Richard Stearns sided with 25 states and the District of Columbia which sued the administration.

A federal judge has ruled against enforcing a new rule by the administration of US President Donald Trump that would require chronically ill people on Medicaid, a public health insurance programme for low-income individuals, to prove themselves “medically frail” to qualify for work exemptions.

US District Judge Richard Stearns blocked the rule on Thursday, siding with 25 states and the District of Columbia, which had sued the Trump administration in June over the change, arguing that it unlawfully limits exemptions for people with serious medical conditions.

The law says the definition of medically frail must include people who are blind or disabled, have substance use disorders or disabling mental disorders, have certain disabilities that significantly impair daily activities, or have serious or complex medical conditions.

But the administration’s rule went further, requiring people in those categories to show that their conditions also “significantly impair” their ability to comply with the law’s work requirements.

The plaintiffs argued that the stricter rule would prevent eligible Americans from accessing the care they need, and that it oversteps the law’s text.

“The states have met their burden of showing irreparable harm for which monetary damages would provide inadequate compensation – they face the burden of costly and intensive alterations to their eligibility verification systems,” Stearns said in his 16-page ruling.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the agency that adopted the rule, declined to comment.

Medicaid is a public health insurance programme for low-income people, funded by state and federal governments.

Starting January 1, 2027, Medicaid expansion enrollees aged 19 to 64 must show that they work or do community service at least 80 hours a month, or are in school at least half the time. There are exceptions for those considered medically frail or in addiction treatment programmes, among others.

Notably, while the ruling will make it easier for some Medicaid recipients with qualifying medical conditions to obtain an exemption from the new work requirements, Stearns’s decision does not strike down the work requirements as unlawful.

Stearns serves in the District of Massachusetts and was appointed by President Bill Clinton.

His ruling upheld two other federal restrictions on how states can verify medical frailty that the states and the District of Columbia had also contested.
sources.headline: US judge blocks Trump’s Medicaid rule forcing ill to prove impairment

sources.body: La crida via xarxes socials per generar aldarulls violents al centre de Barcelona la nit d’aquest dissabte (nit de la Castanyada o de Halloween ) ha posat les institucions, els cossos policials i la justícia en màxima alerta . Precisament per això, l’alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni , ha convocat una Junta Local de Seguretat extraordinària per evitar es repeteixin el pillatge i els actes violents d’una setmana abans . De la trobada n’ha sortit l’acord per estrènyer la col·laboració i redoblar la pressió contra el grup convocant (Blocus-BCN, que diu estar emmirallat en les protestes estudiantils de França ). Per aquest motiu, la Guàrdia Urbana , els Mossos d’Esquadra i els tribunals han expressat el seu “compromís absolut per preservar la convivència i l’ordre públic”, alhora que també han avisat que seran “ implacables amb tots aquells que provoquin destrosses o alterin la convivència”. També et pot interessar Aldarulls de Barcelona: “Els menors estan molt manipulats per les xarxes” Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura Tolerància zero En aquest mateix sentit, han assegurat que hi haurà “ màxima coordinació policial i judicial, amb actuacions preventives i un seguiment continuat dels esdeveniments” per mantenir una actitud de “ tolerància zero ” amb les actituds violentes i conflictives. Malgrat que la Junta Local de Seguretat extraordinària —en què també hi era present la consellera d’Interior, Núria Parlon — no ha posat xifres concretes al desplegament policial, s’espera una gran presència d’agents de la Guàrdia Urbana i dels Mossos d’Esquadra la nit del 31 d’octubre davant de la convocatòria de Blocus-BCN. També et pot interessar Els Mossos, previnguts davant de possibles aldarulls dissabte: “Ens preocupa” Núria Granados Sandra García Prat 2 minuts de lectura De fet, durant aquesta setmana, els Mossos ja han controlat intensivament l’entorn de la plaça d’Espanya , on suposadament també s’havien fet crides a través dels mateixos canals que convoquen la nit de la Castanyada. Els darrers aldarulls van deixar uns 130 detinguts , més de la meitat dels quals són menors d’edat , per a qui la fiscalia ha demanat mesures cautelars . També et pot interessar Què passa quan un menor d’edat és detingut per provocar aldarulls? Els pares han de pagar els danys? Marta Casals Torres 3 minuts de lectura
sources.headline: Urbana, Mossos i jutges intensifiquen la pressió per evitar aldarulls de Blocus la nit de dissabte

sources.body:
Los Mossos d'Esquadra tratan de disolver la convocatoria de actos vandálicos del sábado. / JORDI COTRINA / EPC

La Junta de Seguridad Local reunida este jueves en Barcelona ha advertido de que los cuerpos policiales se mostrarán "implacables" ante los eventuales disturbios previstos para este sábado en la ciudad. Blocus BCN lleva toda la semana llevando a cabo llamamientos vía Telegram y Whatsapp para repetir los actos de la semana pasada, amenaza ante la cual administraciones y autoridades se preparan para actuar.

La Junta se ha convocado de forma extraordinaria, con representantes del Ayuntamiento, con el alcalde Jaume Collboni al frente, y la consejera de Interior, Núria Parlon , así como el delegado del gobierno español, José Crespín , y la presidenta del Tribunal de Instancia de Barcelona, Cristina Ferrando . También han asistido representantes de los diferentes cuerpos policiales y de la Fiscalía. Todos ellos han insistido en la importancia de una respuesta "robusta" ante un fenómeno "sin precedentes".

Los participantes en el encuentro han reafirmado su "compromiso absoluto" para preservar la convivencia y el orden público en la ciudad, ante la posibilidad de que se repitan los actos de pillaje y saqueos del pasado fin de semana. También han subrayado su voluntad de actuar con la "máxima" firmeza si se producen.

Al mismo tiempo, han trasladado un mensaje de "tranquilidad" a la ciudadanía y han apelado a la " responsabilidad " de las familias, recordando que el dispositivo diseñado actuará "desde la máxima coordinación policial y judicial, con actuaciones preventivas y un seguimiento continuo de los acontecimientos que puedan producirse".

Los diferentes poderes públicos han reiterado que tendrán "tolerancia cero" ante cualquier actitud violenta en el espacio público, un requisito "indispensable" para "garantizar la democracia y la libertad". Por tanto, se harán "todos los esfuerzos para preservar estos principios rectores de las sociedades actuales".

Finalmente, ante un escenario "totalmente nuevo" en el que están involucrados menores de edad convocados por personas "que se esconden en el anonimato" de las redes sociales, la Junta Local de Seguridad ha subrayado que los cuerpos policiales y judiciales seguirán exigiendo responsabilidades a sus tutores legales.
sources.headline: La Junta de Seguridad de Barcelona afirma que la policía será “implacable” ante posibles disturbios el fin de semana

stories.headline: Barcelona's Metro Line 2 will close between La Pau and Gorg for a month starting 2 November

sources.body:
A partir de dilluns, 2 de novembre , la línia L2 del metro quedarà tallada parcialment . No circularan trens entre les estacions de La Pau i Gorg durant un mes, fins al 3 de desembre .

Segons han explicat des de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB), cal reparar unes fissures detectades a la plataforma de formigó sobre la qual descansen les vies a l'altura de l' estació d'Artigues-Sant Adrià .

Les esquerdes, que podrien tenir relació amb els aiguats que van caure a principis d'octubre, es van detectar el dia 8 i des d'aleshores s'han pres mesures preventives.

La més important, la reducció de la velocitat dels combois a 15 km/h , fet que ha provocat retards i aglomeracions en hora punta, fins al punt que en alguns moments ha sigut necessari regular l'accés de viatgers a les estacions.

En qualsevol cas, el conseller delegat de TMB, Xavier Flores , ha fet una crida a la tranquil·litat i ha subratllat que tenen "absolutament monitoritzat aquest tram de via".

En cap moment ha suposat un problema de seguretat per als viatgers.

Ara, però, s'han decidit per una solució definitiva que resolgui "el dany estructural" detectat en aquest tram de l'L2 del metro: "Substitució d'aquesta llosa i reforçar la fonamentació per evitar que torni a passar".

Les esquerdes, aparegudes en un tram d'entre 50-60 metres , són en un punt amb canvi d'agulles al túnel que connecta l'estació d'Artigues/Sant Adrià amb la de Sant Roc. Una infraestructura construïda als anys 80 .

Es van trobar en una inspecció rutinària després dels aiguats que van provocar la gran crescuda del riu Besòs entre el 3 i el 5 d'octubre. Es dona el cas que la línia L2 del metro creua per sota del riu .

En aquest sentit, Xavier Flores explica que el túnel on s'han detectat les fissures "és en una zona on hi ha aigua freàtica" :

I podria estar vinculat amb aquest increment del nivell freàtic, que hagi provocat justament el trencament d'aquesta llosa.

El conseller delegat de TMB subratlla, però, que "això no és una ciència exacta".

El tall de la línia L2 entre La Pau i Gorg afectarà prop de 25.000 persones . TMB ha anunciat que habilitarà un servei especial de bus llançadora amb un recorregut proper a les estacions afectades i una freqüència d'entre quatre i nou minuts els dies feiners. El servei es farà amb autobusos articulats.

Tot i això, Flores ha recomanat utilitzar alternatives com les línies de metro L4 , a l'estació de La Pau, i L10 , a Gorg, i també les línies T4, T5 i T6 del tramvia . També ha assenyalat com a alternatives la línia H10 d'autobús , l' R1 de Rodalies i les línies d' autobús B25, M26 i M30 .

Si els treballs avancen segons el calendari previst, el servei de l'L2 es reprendrà amb normalitat la matinada del 4 de desembre .
sources.headline: La línia L2 del metro estarà tallada entre La Pau i Gorg durant un mes a partir de dilluns

sources.body:
La Línea 2 de metro se quedará sin servicio entre las estaciones de La Pau y Gorg durante un mes como máximo, a partir del lunes que viene y en principio hasta el 3 de diciembre. La suspensión del servicio es sobrevenida, a causa de unas fisuras detectadas bajo un tramo de 50 metros que se tendrá que reparar. Las grietas se han localizado en un punto donde existe un cambio de agujas a unos 100 metros de la estación de Artigues/Sant Adrià, dentro del túnel en dirección a Sant Roc . La incidencia, provocada por la presión de la subida del nivel del agua subterránea que se concentra en las inmediaciones del río Besòs, provoca desde hace días una reducción del paso de trenes en la L2, demoras entre un convoy y otro y aglomeraciones de pasajeros en ciertos momentos del día , que han obligado a regular el acceso de viajeros en horas punta en algunas estaciones. "Está provocando una acumulación que no es la idónea, somos conscientes y pedimos disculpas", ha expresado el consejero delegado de Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB), Xavier Flores.

La empresa pública ha anunciado este jueves que el servicio se suspenderá entre cinco paradas a partir del próximo lunes. Desde ese día, se fletará un servicio de bus lanzadera con una frecuencia de paso de cuatro a nueve minutos y que cubrirá un recorrido que conectará las estaciones afectadas, las de La Pau, Verneda, Artigues/Sant Adrià, Sant Roc y Gorg . En todo caso, TMB ha destacado que existen otras alternativas en transporte público en el trecho que se quedará sin metro, como el tranvía o la línea de bus H10.

La compañía ha explicado que las grietas se detectaron el 8 de octubre, en una inspección rutinaria tras los temporales que causaron las grandes crecidas del Besòs entre el 3 y el 5 de octubre. El metro cruza por debajo del río, si bien el punto donde han aparecido las hendiduras no están justo debajo del Besòs.

No obstante, TMB ha explicado que las fisuras se han localizado en una zona situada por debajo del nivel freático, en la que se produjo un incremento del nivel de las aguas subterráneas en los días posteriores a los chubascos intensos. El consejero delegado de la empresa pública, Xavier Flores, ha indicado que no se tiene la certeza de que la causa de la avería sea la crecida del Besòs y sus efectos, si bien ha considerado que existe una "cierta vinculación" entre las secuelas de aquel episodio extraordinario y los daños que llevan a detener la circulación en unas estaciones de la L2 en las que 25.000 personas toman el metro a diario .

Usuarios de la L2 en el andén de la estación de Artigues/Sant Adrià, que está sufriendo retrasos y problemas de frecuencia debido a una incidencia. / JORDI OTIX

El tramo de la L2 donde se han detectado los desperfectos se halla por debajo del nivel de las aguas del subsuelo que existen en torno al Besòs . Se trata de una particularidad de sobras conocida. Sin embargo, ahora se ha producido un deterioro bajo las vías a causa de la filtración de agua del subsuelo. Con las reparaciones puntuales efectuadas de urgencia, el trecho deteriorado se mantiene estabilizado, sin que se aprecien oscilaciones en la losa ni los raíles por el vaivén de trenes. " Cuando el nivel freático sube un metro, la presión pasa a ser de mil kilos más" , ha ilustrado Flores.
sources.headline: La Línea 2 de metro se quedará sin servicio entre La Pau y Gorg del 2 de noviembre al 3 de diciembre

stories.headline: The Catalan government rejects a proposed Empordà wind farm over its landscape impact

sources.body:
Recreació del parc eòlic al pla de la Tallada difosa pels opositors al projecte. / DdG

La Generalitat ha emès una declaració d’impacte ambiental (DIA) desfavorable al projecte eòlic del Pla de la Tallada , al Baix Empordà, per l’ «impacte visual» que tindrien els aerogeneradors sobre l’entorn del massís del Montgrí . Es tracta d’una decisió sorprenent perquè és la primera vegada que es produeix una resolució negativa amb el paisatge com a raó principal.

A més, cal remarcar que es tramiten molt pocs projectes de parc eòlic comercial, i encara menys a l’Empordà, una comarca habitualment reticent a les renovables. El més habitual és que es presentin molts més plans per construir parcs fotovoltaics. Segons EolicCat , l’associació que representa en el sector eòlic català, la decisió és «inèdita» i obre un «escenari d’incertesa» per a altres instal·lacions en vies de tramitació.

El projecte preveia quatre aerogeneradors amb una potència total de 22,8 megawatts (MW) en un territori pla i no de muntanya. Aquest parc, juntament amb el projecte Galatea a l’Albera, encara pendent d’una decisió judicial, havia de ser una de les referències en energia eòlica a les comarques de Girona, un territori que acumula deures pendents en transició energètica. Però l’acord adoptat el 21 d’octubre per la Ponència d’Energies Renovables constata que «els impactes en el fons escènic del Montgrí » no permeten tirar endavant un pla que sí que es considerava viable pel que fa a l’urbanisme i fins i tot quant als efectes ambientals relacionats amb l’ àguila cuabarrada i altres aus.

«És una decisió arbitrària, el projecte ha superat l’avaluació de tots els impactes ambientals objectius i se’n va en orris perquè algú considera que altera un fons escènic», denuncia el president d’EolicCat, Víctor Cusí . Des del punt de vista de l’entitat, el problema no es limita a aquest parc: «Pot arribar a frenar altres infraestructures, des de plantes fotovoltaiques fins a línies d’evacuació o subestacions».

L’associació també qüestiona el moment del procediment en què s’ha aplicat el criteri paisatgístic i, a més, hi veu una contradicció amb la planificació energètica de la Generalitat, recollida en el polèmic PLATER (el Pla Territorial Sectorial per a la Implantació de les Energies Renovables), que en la versió preliminar qualifica d’«apta» la zona on s’ubicarien els aerogeneradors. EolicCat remarca que la protecció paisatgística del Montgrí ja era coneguda i s’havia incorporat a l’elaboració del pla, que combina 141 capes d’informació i més de 50 criteris d’exclusió o ponderació.
sources.headline: El Govern rebutja un parc eòlic a l’Empordà per l’impacte paisatgístic: «És una decisió arbitrària»

sources.body:
Imatge d'arxiu d'un parc eòlic / Jaume Sellart

Defensem l’Empordanet ha respost a les crítiques de la patronal EolicCat sobre el pronunciament ambiental desfavorable de la Generalitat al projecte eòlic de la Tallada d’Empordà . L’associació sosté que l’oposició als quatre aerogeneradors de 200 metres d’alçada previstos al Pla de la Tallada «va molt més enllà del paisatge» i es fonamenta també en les possibles afectacions sobre la qualitat de vida dels veïns, l’agricultura, la biodiversitat i el patrimoni cultural.

L’entitat valora positivament les informacions aparegudes als mitjans sobre la declaració d’impacte ambiental desfavorable, però remarca que encara no disposa del document oficial . Per això, es manté a l’espera de conèixer el contingut íntegre de la resolució i els arguments que la fonamenten.

La resposta arriba després que EolicCat hagi qualificat la decisió «d’arbitrària» i hagi denunciat inseguretat jurídica . Defensem l’Empordanet rebutja que el debat es redueixi a una qüestió de subjectivitat paisatgística i defensa que la protecció del paisatge és una exigència reconeguda per la legislació catalana i els instruments d’ordenació territorial.

Entre els motius del seu rebuig, l’associació assenyala la proximitat dels aerogeneradors a nuclis habitats i masies . Expressa preocupació pel soroll, els infrasons, les ombres intermitents i la il·luminació nocturna, així com per les afectacions de les línies d’evacuació elèctrica.

També adverteix de l’ocupació i transformació de sòl agrícola que comportarien els fonaments, els accessos i les infraestructures associades. Segons l’entitat, cal avaluar els possibles efectes sobre els drenatges, els aqüífers i el comportament hidrològic d’una plana amb zones inundables.

En l’àmbit agrari, Defensem l’Empordanet considera que la implantació del projecte en terres d’alt valor productiu entra en contradicció amb les inversions públiques destinades a modernitzar el regadiu de la Comunitat de Regants de Colomers , que també s’hi ha oposat. L’associació qüestiona, a més, la viabilitat econòmica del parc per les condicions del recurs eòlic i alerta de possibles repercussions sobre el turisme rural, les activitats locals i el valor dels habitatges.

L’entitat també situa entre les seves preocupacions els riscos per a les aus migratòries, les espècies protegides , com l’àliga cuabarrada, i els ratpenats. Remarca que l’emplaçament és pròxim al Parc Natural del Montgrí i a espais de protecció de les aus.

Pel que fa al paisatge i al patrimoni cultural, sosté que els quatre aerogeneradors alterarien les visuals de la plana de l’Empordanet i del massís del Montgrí, així com l’entorn de Bellcaire, del castell i de l’església de Santa Maria de la Tallada i del Rec del Molí.

L’associació ha qüestionat igualment la tramitació del projecte en quatre expedients i reclama una avaluació conjunta dels impactes acumulatius, a més d’una justificació de la idoneïtat de l’emplaçament i de les alternatives.

Defensem l’Empordanet recorda que, a la consulta popular celebrada a la Tallada el desembre de 2025, el 95,68% dels votants es van pronunciar contra el projecte . A aquest resultat hi afegeix el rebuig expressat pels ajuntaments afectats i pels regants.
sources.headline: Defensem l'Empordanet respon a EolicCat: «L'oposició al macroparc eòlic de la Tallada va molt més enllà del paisatge»

stories.headline: Sant Feliu de Guíxols opens Catalonia's first cooperative housing project for older residents

sources.body:
Inauguració del primer habitatge cooperatiu per a gent gran de Catalunya a Sant Feliu de Guíxols. / Juan Luis Campoy - Sostre Cívic

Sant Feliu de Guíxols ha inaugurat aquest dijous Walden XXI, el primer projecte d’habitatge cooperatiu en cessió d’ús específic per a gent gran que entra en funcionament a Catalunya , segons Sostre Cívic , la cooperativa que l’impulsa i gestiona. La rehabilitació de l’antic hotel Jecsalis , al centre del municipi, ha permès crear un espai per a una quarantena de persones que han decidit envellir en comunitat, amb autonomia, suport mutu i una organització col·lectiva de les cures.

L’entrega de claus marca l’inici de la convivència després de vuit anys de treball del grup impulsor . L’edifici disposa de 31 unitats de convivència i combina habitatges privatius amb prop de 800 metres quadrats d’espais compartits. Entre aquests hi ha cuina i menjador comunitari, biblioteca, bugaderia, sales polivalents, tallers i espais exteriors.

Les persones que hi viuran han participat tant en el disseny dels espais com en la definició de l’organització comunitària. Durant els darrers anys, han treballat els acords i les responsabilitats compartides que han de sostenir la convivència, en paral·lel a la compra, el finançament i les obres de rehabilitació.

El projecte vol donar resposta a la solitud no desitjada i mantenir la capacitat de decisió de les persones grans sobre la seva vida. En aquest model, la propietat de l’immoble es manté en mans de la cooperativa i els socis disposen d’un dret d’ús estable a preu de cost. La fórmula preserva els habitatges com a patrimoni col·lectiu per a futurs residents.

Aquest dijous s'ha fet la inauguració i l'entrega de claus de l'edifici. / Juan Luis Campoy - Sostre Cívic

La rehabilitació ha comptat amb el cofinançament de Caixa Enginyers i Fiare Banca Ètica , que el novembre de 2024 van formalitzar una operació d’uns sis milions d’euros. La Fundació Seira també hi va contribuir amb un aval que va facilitar la viabilitat de l’operació.

L’Ajuntament de Sant Feliu de Guíxols ha facilitat el canvi d’ús de l’antic hotel a habitatge amb serveis per a gent gran. El projecte també ha rebut suport de la Generalitat a través de programes de foment de l’economia social i d’una convocatòria per a equipaments cooperatius destinats a persones grans.

La rehabilitació integral ha permès passar d’una qualificació energètica E a una A , amb millores en l’aïllament tèrmic, aerotèrmia, generació d’energia renovable, monitoratge dels consums i recuperació d’aigües grises. La comunitat energètica de Walden XXI ha rebut finançament del Ministeri per a la Transició Ecològica a través de l’Institut per a la Diversificació i Estalvi de l’Energia (IDAE).

Més de 200 persones han assistit a la inauguració, celebrada davant de l’edifici, a la carretera de Girona. L’acte ha inclòs els parlaments, l’entrega d’una clau simbòlica al grup impulsor i una visita als espais comunitaris.

La presidenta de la junta del projecte, Aurora Moreno , ha expressat la voluntat que Walden XXI sigui un referent per a futures iniciatives i ha assegurat que la casa estarà oberta a la vila. Per la seva banda, el soci impulsor Josep Maria Ricart ha reclamat suport públic per estendre el model: «Necessitem suport públic en forma de finançament, sòl, patrimoni i canvis legals per fer realitat més projectes com aquest».
sources.headline: Sant Feliu de Guíxols estrena el primer habitatge cooperatiu per a gent gran de Catalunya
